selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: S. 3738, known as the MORE WATER Act, amends the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act and other water laws to reauthorize large-scale water recycling and reuse programs, authorize support for environmental restoration and endangered species, alter financial ceilings on certain water projects, and set up a process to deauthorize inactive Bureau of Reclamation projects.

affected_groups.effect: Involved in carrying out feasibility studies, water recycling projects, environmental monitoring, and managing the deauthorization process for inactive projects.
Subject to updated funding caps for water recycling projects and required to provide sufficient funding or seek congressional action if sponsoring projects listed for deauthorization.
affected_groups.group: Local Project Sponsors and Non-Federal Entities

key_provisions: Amends the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act to include feasibility studies for large-scale water recycling and reuse projects and extends program authorities.
Raises the ceiling on the Federal share for water recycling projects from $20,000,000 at October 1996 prices to $50,000,000 in December 2025 prices, with annual Consumer Price Index adjustments.

Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to undertake or support activities during fiscal years 2028 through 2032 for habitat restoration, fish passage, monitoring, and temperature modeling for the Great Salt Lake, other saline inland lakes, and the Sacramento River system.

Establishes a process requiring the Secretary of the Interior to publish interim and final deauthorization lists of Bureau of Reclamation projects that have not received funding for specified periods, leading to their deauthorization unless certain exceptions apply.
missing_information: Specific funding amounts for large-scale water recycling and reuse programs or water conveyance programs were present only in deleted text and omitted from the final reported text provisions.
Exact overall fiscal impact numbers for the newly authorized programs are incomplete in the provided source text.
summary_detail.plain_summary: S. 3738, known as the MORE WATER Act, amends the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act and other water laws to reauthorize large-scale water recycling and reuse programs, authorize support for environmental restoration and endangered species, alter financial ceilings on certain water projects, and set up a process to deauthorize inactive Bureau of Reclamation projects.
summary_detail.significance: The bill impacts federal water management policy by extending funding and programmatic authorities for water recycling, habitat restoration, and environmental monitoring under the Bureau of Reclamation while culling inactive infrastructure projects from federal authorization lists.
